answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk with 14 days to a non-auto-renewing primary contract and the line at 94% with zero buffer. That rules out deferral (c5 was non-critical and month-to-month is unverified here) and makes a primary switch unsafe until c2's 'quick onboarding' is checked against this window. Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so negotiate_terms is unlikely to hit the 18% cut and could burn the only decision. Pending archive checks, renewing the incumbent (c1) is the only action that clearly preserves continuity; TCO still includes disruption, which a failed cutover would dominate. Flagging downstream line-stop risk. Not treating c2 or c1 as settled until verified.
